transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19 16:00 PT | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Amanda Ruiz (CISO - Silvergate), Mark Thompson (VP Eng), Eli Park (Cloud Architect)

Summary: Preliminary security posture discovery focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Customer is primarily concerned about SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs and long-term data retention/encryption/KMS. Redwood to send certs and architecture docs; SE to provide sizing and benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Compliance: SOC 2, ISO 27001, data residency
- Identity: SSO, SAML, SCIM, RBAC
- Observability & audit logs: retention, export, SIEM integration
- Encryption and KMS: key ownership, BYOK, HSM
- Deployment modes: hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Next steps: certs, architecture diagrams, demo/benchmarks

Action items (captured verbally in call): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam Chen: Alright everyone thanks for joining, this is Liam from Redwood, uh I'm the account exec on this. With me is Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Priya N.: hey all, thanks for taking the time. We'll keep this focused on your security questions and how the different deployment options map to controls.
[00:14] Amanda Ruiz: Great thanks. To kick off, high level — we run regulated financial workloads, so SOC 2 and ISO are table stakes. We're evaluating whether hosted is acceptable or if we need Dedicated or private run in our VPC. Key questions: certificates, separation, and key management.
[00:29] Mark Thompson: Yeah and, um, we need to understand audit trail fidelity — i.e. logs with user identifiers, API calls, admin actions, retention windows and the ability to ship to Splunk/Datadog.
[00:42] Eli Park: Also SSO is critical. We use Okta and require SAML + SCIM provisioning. RBAC must map to our groups, not just basic roles.
[00:52] Priya N.: Totally. Quick overview: Redwood Hosted is our fully-managed API with SOC 2 compliance and optional enterprise contracts. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with predictable capacity and isolation; it's still our managed control plane but you get dedicated infra. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you a private control plane and can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem for air-gapped needs.
[01:12] Amanda: Do you have ISO 27001 as well? And can we get the certs?
[01:16] Liam: Yes we are ISO 27001 certified, and we can share both SOC 2 Type II and ISO certificates. I'll send those after the call, plus our security whitepaper.
[01:25] Eli: For KMS, is it BYOK? Can we use our KMS/HSM? We can't have Redwood controlling keys for certain workloads.
[01:33] Priya: Good question. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and we integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated and Private. There are a couple of models: shared service with customer-managed CMKs, or full BYOK for private deployments. On Hosted there is an option for customer-managed keys via a customer key store in some clouds — I'll follow up with specifics.
[01:51] Mark: How about audit logs — are they immutable? Can we stream them to our SIEM?
[01:56] Priya: Yes, audit logs for admin and API calls are available and can be exported in real time to S3 or streamed to a SIEM using our log forwarder. Retention is configurable; default retention in Hosted is 90 days, but for enterprise plans we support longer retention or exporting to your storage.
[02:12] Amanda: What about data at rest encryption for models and cached KV? We can't have persistent PII in logs or caches.
[02:18] Priya: We encrypt at rest for model artifacts and KV cache. For dedicated/private you can bring your own keys. For Hosted we have automatic prefix/KV caching but you can opt out or configure TTLs and redaction policies. We'll send a doc with recommended TTLs and cache redaction patterns.
[02:36] Liam: Quick clarification: when you say "can't have keys controlled", is that for all workloads or just regulated buckets?
[02:42] Amanda: Regulated buckets. We can tolerate Redwood-managed keys for low sensitivity but regulated flows need BYOK and HSM-backed keys.
[02:50] Priya: Understood. For dedicated and private we support linking to your KMS and HSM via customer-managed CMKs; for on-prem we can also integrate with your HSM appliances.
[02:59] Eli: SSO specifics — we use Okta, SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning and require role mapping to AD groups. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[03:08] Priya: RBAC in Redwood supports customizable roles and you can map SAML assertions/SCIM groups to roles. Admin actions are logged. There are built-in roles (admin, dev, reader) and you can create scoped roles with permissions for model deploy, rollback, billing visibility, etc.
[03:25] Mark: Any multi-tenant leakage concerns with Hosted? We've heard about KV cache cold starts leading to cross-tenant residues.
[03:32] Priya: We take isolation seriously. Raw KV caching in Hosted is namespace-isolated per customer; however if you want physical isolation that's where Dedicated helps — you get reserved GPU pools and isolated cache. Private gives you complete control. We do prefix-sanitization and strict tenancy checks but we will share the design doc that shows how caching and isolation works.
[03:53] Amanda: What about penetration test results and third-party audits?
[03:57] Liam: We run annual pen tests and can share a summary. We also have third-party attestation that is included in our enterprise pack. I'll put the pen test redacted summary in the security bundle.
[04:08] Eli: Network setup — if we go Dedicated in our cloud region, can we place instances in our VPC with private ENIs?
[04:14] Priya: Yes, for Private deployments we do customer VPC peering and private ENIs. For Dedicated we have options: either a managed dedicated subnet in our cloud with private connectivity or a customer VPC with a peering/private link depending on the cloud. We'll include a sample network diagram.
[04:32] Mark: Any SLA on audit log delivery and availability? We need to show auditors that logs are retained and available for X years.
[04:40] Priya: SLA for log availability is part of the enterprise contract. By default Hosted retention is shorter; for audit purposes we recommend exporting logs to your long-term storage (S3/Glacier) — Redwood can automate exports to your bucket with lifecycle rules.
[04:55] Amanda: Data residency — some customers require EU-resident data only. Do you support region pinning?
[04:59] Liam: Yes, region pinning is supported across Hosting and Dedicated. For Private you can obviously keep everything in-region. We maintain data residency controls and contractual addenda for data residency.
[05:10] Eli: One small quibble — what's the model for model artifacts and versioning? Are older checkpoints retained and who can access them?
[05:17] Priya: Model artifacts are stored encrypted. Access is limited to orchestration services and audited. You can pin versions and we keep an immutable artifact store; retention and purging policies are configurable per customer.
[05:28] Mark: On SAML, do you support signed assertions and audience/recipient restrictions? We lock down tokens tightly.
[05:34] Priya: Yes, we support signed SAML assertions, audience and recipient checks, and can configure assertion lifetimes. We'll capture the technical config in the follow-up doc.
[05:45] Amanda: Billing visibility — we want token-level traces for chargebacks. Is that in audit logs?
[05:50] Liam: Yes we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns via the Console and we can include token-level traces in the logs for chargeback. We can also push usage events to your billing system via webhook.
[06:03] Eli: Are there any known limitations for FedRAMP or higher regulated environments?
[06:07] Liam: We don't currently hold FedRAMP. For FedRAMP-level workloads we recommend Private on-prem or our Dedicated private instances in a compliant cloud with the proper attestation; this is something our compliance team can scoping with you if needed.
[06:21] Mark: Okay good. Can we run a PoC to validate latency and cost with a red-team of prompts?
[06:25] Priya: Yes, typical POC pattern is a 2-4 week pilot on Dedicated or Hosted with workload mirroring. We'll provide benchmark scripts and sample configs. For regulated samples we can do VPC/Dedicated pilot so data never leaves your network.
[06:40] Amanda: One question on retention: auditors ask for data retention policy for logs and for prompt/response pairs used for model tuning. Do you store prompts?
[06:50] Priya: By default we do ephemeral storage for prompts used in inference unless you opt in for logging to help debugging or for model improvement. For Hosted we have opt-in for data usage. For Enterprise we can disable data usage for model tuning and ensure redaction. We'll send our data retention matrix.
[07:10] Liam: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO certs, pen-test summary, security whitepaper, network diagrams, and the SE will send sizing/benchmark configs. We'll schedule a follow-up to walk through Dedicated demo and a potential pilot.
[07:23] Amanda: That works. Also please include the SLA page and the audit log export instructions.
[07:28] Liam: Will do.
[07:31] Priya: Anything else on encryption?
[07:33] Eli: One more: key rotation and split key policies — we require rotation every 90 days and custodial separation for production keys. Can Redwood support that?
[07:41] Priya: Yes, for BYOK we defer to your KMS rotation policy. We can also integrate with an external HSM that supports split-key. We'll include the HSM integration notes.
[07:51] Mark: Great. Looking forward to the docs.
[07:53] Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up early next week with the package.
[07:58] Amanda: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
